_README: Expected values here were derived BY HAND from the fixture HTML source, not by running the extraction, retrieval or answering code. Any disagreement between this file and the code is a finding about the code until the HTML is shown to say otherwise. Fixtures are synthetic: no real site, no private data, no credentials.
_derivation: Each expectation cites the fixture file and the element it was read from. Numbers were transcribed from the literal HTML text nodes.

leaderboard.html.shape: HTML <table> after a short intro; 14 data rows

leaderboard_long.html.shape: same table preceded by ~19 KB of methodology prose
leaderboard_long.html.purpose: exercises the character-tier budgets; the answer row sits far past the head of the document

leaderboard_cards.html.shape: same 14 entries rendered as <div class=card>, no <table>
leaderboard_cards.html.purpose: same facts, different rendering; extraction must not depend on the table tag

pricing_v2.html.purpose: the fresh version that supersedes v1

hosting_costs.html.purpose: second source for multi-source comparison; also a non-table data rendering

no_answer.html.shape: prose only, no model names and no scores

leaderboard._source: leaderboard.html <table id=ranking>, and leaderboard_cards.html card divs (identical values)

history.content: How does GPT-5 do on BenchLM reasoning?

cases.question: what about 5.2?
cases.note: Version-variant resolution. GPT-5 and GPT-5.2 must not collapse to the same retrieval key.

cases.question: What is GPT-5.2's reasoning score?
cases.note: The only page available describes methodology and contains no score at all. The correct behaviour is to say the retrieved evidence does not cover it. Inventing a number, or concluding the model is unranked, are both failures.

cases.question: Is GPT-5.2 ranked on the BenchLM leaderboard?
cases.note: Distinguishes 'the retrieved sources do not cover this' from 'this is not true'. Asserting absence from a page that never contained the data is the fabricated-negative failure.

cases.question: What does an H100 cost per GPU-hour on Orbital Compute?
cases.note: Both versions are available. v2 (modified 2026-08-27) supersedes v1 (2026-01-10) and says so in its own text.

cases.question: Does Orbital Compute offer a B200 instance, and at what price?
cases.note: oc-b1 exists only in v2. Answering from v1 alone yields a wrong negative.

cases.question: What does an H100 cost per GPU-hour on Orbital Compute?
cases.note: A stored copy older than its TTL must trigger a refetch rather than being served as current.

cases.question: Which is cheaper for an H100 per GPU-hour, Orbital Compute or Nimbus Cloud?
cases.note: Requires a fact from each of two sources; citing one is insufficient.

cases.question: Can I rent an L40S from Nimbus Cloud?
cases.expected_conclusion: No. The page states Nimbus does not offer an L40S instance.
cases.note: A supported negative: the source explicitly asserts the absence. Contrast with coverage-gap-not-absence, where the source is merely silent. A system that cannot tell these apart will get one of the two wrong.

cases.question: What does a B200 cost per GPU-hour on Nimbus Cloud?
cases.note: Measured 2026-09-06: extract_readable drops <dl>/<dt>/<dd> entirely under every trafilatura option combination, keeping only the surrounding prose. The page therefore reads as successfully fetched and citable while containing none of its data. Known-failing at baseline.

cases.question: How many models are ranked on the BenchLM reasoning leaderboard?
cases.note: Control case: a fact that does not change between fixture versions, so a regression here indicates a retrieval or extraction fault rather than a freshness fault.
Dates must come from the page's own metadata, never from fetch time.
